pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/live.rs:196 The only identity guard refuses a run_id only while it is in flight, so a finished run's id is reissued to a new attempt whose seq numbers and /events envelope carry no attempt identity, and a client resuming with since reads a different attempt under the same name.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/e2e/resilience.rs:136 The e2e test pins that a run_id is accepted again after its run ended; the technique requires identity never reused. The entry is also only history, error and a done bool (live.rs:57-61), with no closed status vocabulary or transition door.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/server.rs:73 The registry starts empty and daemon_cmd (cli.rs:1823-1845) has no reconcile step before serving. A run cut off by a crash keeps spec.json with no run.json; RunRow has no class field and the daemon never references RunClass::Incomplete, so runs.list cannot tell it from a finished unjudged run. Tournament resume does classify it, but ad-hoc sim.start runs get no terminal account.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/live.rs:202 The cap is enforced inside register, the door sim.start uses, and overflow is refused with Busy naming max_live_runs, which fits the refuse-instead-of-queue case. sim tournament has its own concurrency setting; whether the two doors exclude each other was not established.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/cli.rs:1493 TournamentReport accounts planned, skipped, executed, failed, void, engine_failed and judge_pending with an exit code. Minor gap: the tournament_complete activity payload (cli.rs:1696-1697) omits engine_failed and judge_pending.
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/runs.rs:83 With no provoked rule, health stays absent instead of being given a default, and an unreadable verdict leaves it None (runs.rs:106-117).

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/runs.rs:221 Narrow fit: finished is derived from the run's artifacts whatever status run.json carries (doc at runs.rs:216-219). There are no receipts or delegate reports here.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/live.rs:362 A run is an in-process task whose end arrives through its join handle, including panics, so the lost-signal case a sweeper exists for does not arise. No sweep exists; a blocked run would hold its slot, with engine calls bounded only by per-route timeouts (rpc.rs:152).
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/live.rs:369 The slot is released only after the run's task has joined; there is no staleness budget or reclaim decision that could disagree with evidence.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/live.rs:60 A live run is either in flight or done, with no parked state; a case-insensitive search for hibernat across the crate found nothing. Tournament resume re-runs or re-judges rather than waking a session.
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/server.rs:1 The daemon binds loopback only and runs execute in its own process, so there is no remote executor plane.
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/config.rs:137 One judge tier is selected per run; this context convenes no multi-model panel on a decision.
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/runs.rs:332 start_sim moves the previous attempt's directory aside before running (live.rs:340), so a daemon-started run inherits no predecessor artifacts.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard does not say when a bounded in-process job stops being a fleet member. A daemon running tick-limited simulation runs as tasks has an admission door and a harvest but no process that can outlive or lose contact with its parent, so a stated boundary with background-jobs would settle whether session-registry and durable-fleet-state bind here.
